recognize_zh: A 圖血液抹片可見大量小而緻密、缺乏中央淡染區的球形紅血球（spherocytes）與多染性紅血球、有核紅血球，提示溶血；B 圖角膜周緣褐色環（箭頭，Kayser-Fleischer ring），兩者合併急性肝衰竭即指向猛爆性威爾森氏症（Wilson disease）。
features: Polychromatophilic macrocytic red cells indicating reticulocytosis
Scattered irregularly contracted/crenated red cells; no schistocytes or agglutination evident
Clinical photo: golden-brown peripheral corneal ring (Kayser-Fleischer ring, arrow)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (A) shows numerous spherocytes and irregularly contracted red cells lacking central pallor, accompanied by polychromatophilic macrocytes and occasional nucleated red blood cells, indicating brisk hemolysis with a marrow response. Red cell agglutination and prominent schistocytes are not seen in this field. The eye photograph (B) shows a brownish ring at the limbal margin of the cornea (arrow), consistent with a Kayser-Fleischer ring. In a young patient with jaundice and rapidly progressive liver failure, the combination of Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia and Kayser-Fleischer rings is consistent with fulminant Wilson disease, in which massive copper release causes oxidative red cell injury.

ddx.vs: Warm AIHA also produces spherocytes and polychromasia but has a positive direct antiglobulin test and lacks Kayser-Fleischer rings or acute liver failure.
HS causes chronic lifelong spherocytic hemolysis with family history and abnormal EMA binding, not abrupt hemolysis with fulminant hepatic failure.
Clostridium perfringens toxin causes explosive microspherocytic hemolysis with sepsis, but serum copper, ceruloplasmin and eye findings are normal.

ddx.dx: Spur cell (acanthocytic) anemia of liver disease
ddx.vs: Advanced cirrhosis produces acanthocytes with irregular spiny projections rather than smooth round spherocytes.

captions: A: Peripheral smear with spherocytes, polychromasia and nucleated RBCs
B: Kayser-Fleischer ring at the corneal limbus (arrow)
